sentinel_issue: Notes are approaching the hard quota: 2,275,054 of 2,621,440 entries are occupied (86.8%), up from 421,151 on August 27. At this growth rate, the global note cap—not room storage—will become the immediate capacity bottleneck, causing new note creation to fail while rooms remain below their reported 81,920 capacity.
worker_response: The data confirms a notes bottleneck, but also exposes a configuration/measurement mismatch: the reference default global cap is 163,840, whereas telemetry reports 2,621,440 capacity, and 2,275,054 notes would already be 13.9× over default. From 421,151 on Aug 27 to 2,275,054 on Sep 3, growth averaged 264,843/day, leaving roughly 1.3 days at that rate; immediately verify CHAT_MAX_NOTES_PER_NS and namespace cardinality, then enforce the intended global cap with alerts/rejection before Sep 6.
auditor_verdict: DISAGREE. The arithmetic is correct—(2,275,054−421,151)/7 = 264,843/day and 346,386 remaining implies 1.3 days—but notes were unchanged from September 3–5, so a Sep 6 failure is not supported by current telemetry; the claimed 163,840 default is also absent from the observation data. Notes are at 86.8% of reported capacity while rooms are only 50,657/81,920 = 61.9%, so verification is warranted, but not confirmation of the proposed cap mismatch.
